concepts.name: Hebbian Learning
concepts.short_description: Neurons that fire together wire together; activity-dependent synaptic strengthening, LTP/LTD.

concepts.name: Information Theory
concepts.short_description: Quantification of information, entropy, and channel capacity; Shannon entropy, mutual information, KL divergence.

concepts.name: Morphogenesis
concepts.short_description: Self-organized pattern formation in development; Turing patterns, morphogen gradients, reaction-diffusion.

entropy H, mutual information I, KL divergence

I symmetric and invariant under invertible reparametrization

any scale where a probability can be defined

hypotheses.statement: Plastic transport: the diffusion couplings between neighbouring cells are themselves Hebbian, strengthened by co-activation of the activator; the pattern carves the medium it runs on, so a dynamic Turing pattern can become written into structure. Experiment: re-run pattern formation from fresh noise on the learned coupling graph and test recall.

Hebbian readout of positional information: cells must decode position from noisy gradients; a local Hebbian competitive readout either reaches or falls short of the information-theoretic bound (bits of positional information set by gradient noise). Experiment: bits decoded by Hebbian readout vs optimal decoder vs integration time.

Feature-map formation is a Turing instability in weight space: Hebbian positive feedback is the activator, normalization/lateral inhibition the inhibitor. The open question is whether the selected wavelength is set by the kernel (morphogenesis) or by input covariance structure (information). Experiment: vary input correlation length and track map wavelength.

Development as a lossy decompression whose missing bits are supplied by the environment via Hebbian correlation: phenotype information = genome bits + bits absorbed during growth. Experiment: grow the same developmental program under different input statistics and partition I(structure; genome) vs I(structure; environment).

A plastic reaction-diffusion medium as associative memory: several patterns stored as attractors of the coupled field, with a capacity in bits per cell limited by locality. Experiment: sequentially store patterns, recall from corrupted cue, measure capacity vs a local Hopfield control.

Morphogenetic error correction: Hebbian consolidation of neighbour agreements creates redundancy that lets a lesioned pattern regrow; the redundancy is measurable as a code distance. Experiment: lesion size vs recovered bits, with and without consolidated couplings.

Dissipative-to-structural transition: a pattern maintained by continuous flux is costly; Hebbian consolidation converts it into a frozen structure whose maintenance costs less per stored bit. Experiment: dissipation per maintained bit before vs after consolidation, and persistence after flux shut-off.

Coupling-plastic reaction-diffusion: edge diffusion coefficients D_ij evolve as dD_ij = eta*(a_i*a_j - theta) - lambda*(D_ij - D0), clipped to [Dmin,Dmax]; activator co-activity opens channels, anti-correlation closes them.

concept_contributions.Information Theory: the criterion for what the medium retains: I(coupling graph; past pattern)
concept_contributions.Morphogenesis: the activator-inhibitor dynamics that generate the correlated activity to be written

knockouts.Hebbian Learning: couplings fixed: pattern is purely dynamic, forgets on reset
knockouts.Information Theory: mechanism still runs; only the measurement disappears (weak dependency: info theory is observer here)
knockouts.Morphogenesis: no symmetry breaking, activity uniform, couplings drift uniformly

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Hand-imposed spatial heterogeneity in D (a prepattern) that pins spots, with no learning at all.

questions.what_exists: cells with activator/inhibitor state; plastic edges
questions.what_persists: the coupling graph after the pattern is gone
questions.what_is_selected: which edges survive (those inside co-active domains)
questions.what_can_reproduce: the pattern, when re-run from noise on learned couplings
questions.what_can_transfer: learned coupling graph could be transplanted onto a new medium
questions.distinguishing_observable: recall correlation of re-grown pattern with original, above permuted-coupling null

hypotheses.statement: Oja-normalized Hebbian weights on a sheet with short-range excitatory lateral coupling and long-range inhibition generate a periodic feature map whose wavelength is jointly set by the lateral kernel and the input correlation length.

concept_contributions.Information Theory: input covariance whose principal modes Hebbian learning extracts
concept_contributions.Morphogenesis: activator-inhibitor lateral kernel producing mode selection

knockouts.Hebbian Learning: no map; weights stay at initialization
knockouts.Information Theory: with white input the kernel alone sets wavelength (plain Turing)
knockouts.Morphogenesis: without lateral kernel each unit learns the same top PC; no spatial pattern

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Plain Turing instability of the lateral kernel; input statistics irrelevant.

questions.what_exists: sheet of units with feedforward weights
questions.what_is_selected: the Fourier mode with largest growth rate
questions.what_can_transfer: map wavelength law across input ensembles
questions.distinguishing_observable: slope of log wavelength vs log input correlation length (kernel-only predicts zero)

hypotheses.statement: Each cell has K readout units receiving noisy concentrations of two opposing gradients; competitive Hebbian learning (winner-take-most with Oja decay) allocates readout tuning curves where positional information per unit is highest, approaching the positional-information bound set by gradient noise.

concept_contributions.Hebbian Learning: unsupervised competitive allocation of tuning curves
concept_contributions.Information Theory: the bound (bits of positional information) that defines success

knockouts.Morphogenesis: no gradient, no positional information to decode

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Uniform tiling of tuning curves in concentration space (fixed quantizer) giving similar bits.

questions.what_is_selected: readout units that win more samples
questions.what_can_transfer: trained readout to a new gradient shape
questions.distinguishing_observable: fraction of optimal-decoder bits achieved vs uniform quantizer

hypotheses.statement: Engram tiling: a 2D plastic RD medium with coupling plasticity (M1) stores several distinct patterns sequentially; each becomes a basin of the coupled field and is recalled from a partial cue.

concept_contributions.Hebbian Learning: writing each pattern into the couplings
concept_contributions.Information Theory: capacity in bits per plastic edge
concept_contributions.Morphogenesis: the field dynamics that do pattern completion

knockouts.Morphogenesis: without reaction nonlinearity recall is just diffusion blurring

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Nearest-neighbour Hopfield network: this is probably a local Hopfield net in disguise.

questions.what_can_transfer: stored pattern set to a new medium by copying couplings
questions.distinguishing_observable: capacity and basin size relative to a local Hopfield control with equal edge count

hypotheses.statement: Fossilization transition: after a consolidation period the reaction flux is shut off or the fields reset, and the pattern persists or re-forms only because couplings now carry it; a critical consolidation time t* separates forgetting from retention.

concept_contributions.Information Theory: measured bits retained after flux shut-off

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Slow relaxation: long intrinsic timescale of the fields makes the pattern appear to persist.

questions.what_can_transfer: fossilized structure as prepattern for another medium
questions.distinguishing_observable: sharp threshold in retained bits vs consolidation time (sigmoid with finite t*)

hypotheses.statement: Neighbour-consensus repair: consolidated couplings bias a lesioned region to re-grow the original pattern rather than a new random one; recovered bits scale with the redundancy stored in intact border couplings.

knockouts.Hebbian Learning: lesion regrows a random pattern (same wavelength, wrong phase)

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Boundary pinning: the intact surrounding pattern alone fixes phase in the lesion.

questions.distinguishing_observable: recovery with couplings inside lesion scrambled vs intact, controlling for border pinning

hypotheses.statement: Hebbian-biased mutation: the offspring's initial coupling template is mutated preferentially on edges that were co-active during the parent's development (a Lamarckian-ish channel).

concept_contributions.Hebbian Learning: co-activity statistics used as mutation bias
concept_contributions.Information Theory: bits transferred from parent's experience to offspring genome
concept_contributions.Morphogenesis: the developing pattern that generates co-activity

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Plain inheritance of acquired couplings (copying), not a mutation bias. Three-way dependency weak.

questions.distinguishing_observable: rate of adaptation vs uniform mutation at equal mutation load

hypotheses.statement: Selection on positional-information bits: a population of developmental programs is selected for I(cell fate; position) under noise, and Hebbian plasticity during development is a heritable parameter.

concept_contributions.Hebbian Learning: within-life plasticity that may be selected for or against

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Direct optimization of a threshold-reading decoder; plasticity irrelevant. Hebbian dependency weak.

questions.what_can_transfer: evolved plasticity to new noise level
questions.distinguishing_observable: whether evolved plasticity rate rises with environmental variability

hypotheses.statement: Timing-asymmetric Hebbian coupling (STDP-like) under travelling morphogen waves writes an antisymmetric component D_ij - D_ji aligned with wave direction, creating a polarity field (a tissue arrow) from purely temporal order.

concept_contributions.Information Theory: directional information: transfer entropy along edges

knockouts.Morphogenesis: no waves, no order to record

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Advection/drift term in the RD equation giving the same asymmetry without learning.

questions.what_can_transfer: polarity as bias for later patterning
questions.distinguishing_observable: polarity alignment with wave history after waves stop

hypotheses.statement: Anti-Hebbian lateral decorrelation acts as the long-range inhibitor: cells whose outputs are correlated strengthen mutual inhibition, producing spaced fates whose spacing equals the decorrelation length (whitening = spacing pattern).

knockouts.Hebbian Learning: fixed inhibition: spacing set by kernel only
knockouts.Morphogenesis: without spatial embedding, decorrelation gives no spatial pattern

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Fixed lateral inhibition (Notch-Delta-like) with no learning.

questions.distinguishing_observable: spacing tracks input correlation length under learning but not under fixed inhibition

hypotheses.statement: Morphogenesis as physical PCA: a plastic tissue perturbed by structured noise settles on the Fourier mode that matches the top eigenmode of the perturbation covariance, so the pattern is a readout of environmental statistics.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Resonance: linear filter amplifying the input band; overlaps heavily with M2 (possible duplicate).

questions.distinguishing_observable: selected wavenumber vs top eigen-wavenumber across ensembles

hypotheses.statement: Conjunctive positional code: with two orthogonal gradients, Hebbian learning builds conjunctive readout units whose tiling approaches the 2D positional-information bound; units become periodic (grid-like) when the gradients are periodic.

questions.distinguishing_observable: synergy: I(x,y;code) minus sum of separable codes

hypotheses.statement: Segment number set by bits: a growing body adds segments until the positional-information budget per segment drops below one bit; Hebbian reinforcement of segment boundaries prevents boundary drift.

knockouts.Information Theory: no stopping rule, segment count set by length/wavelength

questions.distinguishing_observable: segment count scaling with noise at fixed length (wavelength-only predicts none)

hypotheses.statement: Conserved total coupling per cell (synaptic scaling) plus flux-driven Hebbian reinforcement makes transport channels compete and branch into a hierarchical network that maximizes delivered morphogen information per unit coupling.

concept_contributions.Information Theory: delivered information per unit coupling as the objective the network approaches

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Physarum-style flow reinforcement (known adaptive transport network): very likely familiar in disguise.

hypotheses.statement: Speed-precision law: Hebbian time-averaging of noisy morphogen raises positional bits as 0.5*log2(T) until the gradient's capacity, so developmental speed trades against boundary precision with a predictable exponent.

knockouts.Hebbian Learning: no integration: bits fixed at single-sample level

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Any low-pass filter gives the same law; Hebbian specificity unnecessary.

questions.distinguishing_observable: slope of bits vs log2 T near 0.5 and a ceiling

hypotheses.statement: Sign-flipped plasticity selects pattern morphology: Hebbian coupling (co-activity strengthens) favours spots, anti-Hebbian favours labyrinths, and the transition point is where pattern entropy per cell is maximal.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Plasticity just shifts effective D ratio, which is known to move spot/stripe boundaries.

questions.distinguishing_observable: entropy peak at the morphology transition vs shift of D ratio alone

lenses.name: Coupling-ledger lens
lenses.rationale: If the medium writes patterns into couplings, the coupling graph should be a readable ledger of pattern history.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series of edge couplings D_ij(t) and field snapshots a(t)
lenses.transformation: compute I(D(t); past pattern) and decode past pattern from D alone via re-growth
observables: MI between thresholded couplings and past domain membership
predictedSignals: recall correlation well above permuted-coupling null
lenses.nullExpectation: Permuted couplings (same value histogram) give recall at chance, i.e. matching fresh-noise RD baseline
failureModes: boundary-pinned patterns recur regardless of couplings
MI estimator bias at small cell counts
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Treats structure as memory of dynamics; no other lens reads the coupling graph

lenses.name: Positional-bits lens
lenses.rationale: Positional information is the natural currency tying gradients to readouts.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: cell index x and readout state r(x) across noise samples
lenses.transformation: estimate I(x; r) in bits by binning; compare with optimal Bayesian decoder bits
predictedSignals: Hebbian readout reaches large fraction of optimal
bits grow as ~0.5 log2 T with integration time
lenses.nullExpectation: random fixed readout of equal norm gives substantially fewer bits
failureModes: optimal decoder bound mis-specified if noise model wrong
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Quantifies readout quality rather than pattern shape

lenses.name: Fossilization-clock lens
lenses.rationale: Invented here: measures when a dynamic pattern turns into a structural one.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: consolidation duration t_c and retained recall after flux shut-off/field reset
lenses.transformation: sweep t_c, fit sigmoid of recall vs log t_c
lenses.nullExpectation: smooth, gradual rise proportional to accumulated coupling change (no transition)
failureModes: threshold artifact of clipping bounds Dmin/Dmax
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Distinguishes a phase-like transition from simple accumulation

lenses.name: Wavelength-versus-covariance lens
lenses.rationale: Decides whether pattern scale is kernel-set (morphogenesis) or statistics-set (information).
lenses.sourceRepresentation: spatial power spectrum of learned map; eigen-spectrum of input covariance
lenses.transformation: compare dominant wavenumber k* with kernel-predicted k_T and top eigen-wavenumber k_PC across input ensembles
observables: log-log slope of lambda* vs xi
predictedSignals: k* moves with input correlation length
lenses.nullExpectation: k* = k_T regardless of input statistics (slope ~ 0)
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Only lens that separates the two causes of scale

lenses.name: Wound-bit-accounting lens
lenses.rationale: Invented here: repair counted in bits, separating border pinning from stored memory.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: pattern before lesion, after regrowth; couplings inside/outside lesion
lenses.transformation: bits recovered = I(original lesion region; regrown region), under three conditions: intact couplings, scrambled-inside couplings, fixed-coupling medium
lenses.nullExpectation: intact = scrambled-inside (border pinning explains all recovery)
failureModes: lesion smaller than wavelength trivially recovers
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: Separates two memory sources: neighbours vs stored couplings

lenses.name: Dissipation-per-bit lens
lenses.rationale: Tests the claim that structure is cheaper than flux for holding a pattern.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: reaction flux sum |f(a,h)| over time and retained bits
lenses.transformation: ratio of flux to recalled bits before and after consolidation
failureModes: flux definition arbitrary in toy kinetics

lenses.name: Polarity-arrow lens
lenses.rationale: Invented here: reads temporal order written into asymmetric couplings.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: antisymmetric part of coupling matrix A_ij = D_ij - D_ji
lenses.transformation: correlate local arrow field with past wave direction
observables: mean cosine between arrow and wave direction

experiments.hypothesis: Coupling-plastic RD writes its pattern into edge couplings so that re-running from fresh noise on the learned graph reproduces the original pattern.
experiments.mechanism: Gierer-Meinhardt kinetics on a 48x48 grid, 4-neighbour edges; activator diffusion on edge e is D0*g_e, g_e updated by dg = eta*(a_i*a_j/mean(a)^2 - 1) - lambda*(g-1), clipped [0.2,5].
experiments.intervention: Phase A: 3000 steps with plasticity on (seed s). Phase B: reset fields to uniform plus fresh noise (seed s+1000), plasticity off, run 3000 steps.
experiments.control: Phase B on the uniform graph g=1 (baseline recurrence from boundary pinning).
experiments.positive_control: Phase B on a hand-carved graph with g=5 inside original activator-high domains and 0.2 across domain boundaries.
experiments.observable: Pearson r between z-scored Phase A final activator map and Phase B final activator map.
experiments.success_criterion: Mean r (10 seeds) >= 0.5 and exceeds null-twin mean by >= 0.3, one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.01 over paired seeds; positive control r >= 0.7.
experiments.failure_criterion: Mean r minus null-twin mean < 0.1, or positive control r < 0.5 (world cannot express the effect).
experiments.alternative_explanation: Learned couplings merely lower effective activator diffusion globally, changing wavelength, and boundary effects align patterns.
experiments.null_twin: Same learned g values randomly permuted across edges (identical value histogram and mean), so coupling statistics match but spatial alignment with the pattern is destroyed.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Direct discretized PDE keeps the morphogenetic ontology; no neural network is used; the plastic element is a transport coefficient, not a weight in a learner.
experiments.size: 48x48 cells, 4512 edges, 6000 steps total, 10 seeds x 3 conditions (+positive control)
stupid_explanations: boundary pinning makes any RD run reproduce similar stripes near edges
Pearson r inflated by the shared wavelength (periodic maps correlate by chance at some phases)
clipping bounds create a static prepattern independent of learning
insufficient noise reset so Phase B starts near Phase A state

anomalies.text: cheat r = 1.0 on all seeds but classed not-detected only because reading 4 folds the positive-control clause (>= 0.7) into the success criterion
attempt 1 carved graph (z>0) was one percolating domain; repaired to z>1 cores; positive r rose -0.05 -> 0.28, still < 0.5 (failure_criterion: world cannot express the effect)
learned g in Phase A never reached the 5 clip (0% at max, ~16% at 0.2)

experiments.hypothesis: Competitive Hebbian readout of two noisy opposing gradients recovers most of the optimal positional information, and bits grow with integration time as ~0.5 log2 T up to a ceiling.
experiments.mechanism: 100 cells on a line; gradients c1=exp(-x/20), c2=exp(-(100-x)/20) with multiplicative noise sigma=0.3; K=8 readout units per cell population, winner-take-most Hebbian with Oja decay, trained on 20000 samples; input averaged over T samples.
experiments.intervention: Train Hebbian readout; sweep T in {1,2,4,8,16,32}.
experiments.control: Uniform fixed quantizer tiling (K=8 bins evenly in log-concentration space).
experiments.positive_control: Optimal Bayesian decoder using known noise model.
experiments.observable: I(x; readout) in bits, plug-in estimate with 50000 test samples, Miller-Madow corrected.
experiments.success_criterion: Hebbian bits >= 0.8 x optimal-decoder bits (restricted to K=8 outputs) at T=1, and exceeds null twin by >= 0.5 bits; slope of bits vs log2 T over T<=8 in [0.3,0.7] for 10 seeds.
experiments.failure_criterion: Hebbian bits <= uniform quantizer bits + 0.1, or slope outside [0.15,0.85].
experiments.alternative_explanation: Any quantizer adapted to input density (histogram equalization) gives the same result; Hebbian specificity not needed.
experiments.null_twin: Readout with tuning centres drawn at random from the input range (same K, same widths), destroying learned allocation.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Small population of readout units with explicit gradients; competitive Hebb is a local rule, not a trained network; information measured directly.
experiments.size: 100 cells, 8 units, 20000 train / 50000 test samples, 6 T values, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: MI estimator bias favours whichever readout has more occupied bins
optimal bound computed with wrong noise model making ratio look high
the 0.5 log2 T law follows from Gaussian averaging with no role for Hebb

anomalies.text: CHEAT injected bits exceed log2(8)=3 at some T: injection is not a physically realisable 8-output readout
attainability: clauses (a)+(c) need bits(T=8) >= ~0.8*PC(T=1)+0.9 = 2.684 vs cap 3.0
TREATMENT uses fewer than 8 outputs at T=1 in some seed (min 7)

experiments.hypothesis: Map wavelength formed by Oja-Hebbian learning under a Mexican-hat lateral kernel tracks the input correlation length rather than being fixed by the kernel.
experiments.mechanism: Ring of 128 units, each with feedforward weights from 128 inputs; lateral kernel difference of Gaussians (sigma_e=2, sigma_i=6); inputs Gaussian with spatial correlation length xi.
experiments.intervention: Sweep xi in {1,2,4,8,16}; train 20000 samples each.
experiments.control: Kernel-only prediction k_T (fastest-growing mode of kernel) computed analytically.
experiments.positive_control: Set lateral kernel to identity (no Turing) with structured input: the map should become top-PC dominated, confirming the PCA channel operates.
experiments.observable: dominant wavelength lambda* of the learned preferred-position map, from power spectrum peak.
experiments.success_criterion: Spearman rho(xi, lambda*) >= 0.9 pooled over 5 seeds per xi, and log-log slope >= 0.5; null-twin slope < 0.2.
experiments.failure_criterion: slope < 0.2 in the structured condition (kernel sets wavelength: plain Turing, mechanism reduces to familiar)
experiments.alternative_explanation: Weight smoothing from correlated input simply low-passes the map, lengthening apparent wavelength without mode selection.
experiments.null_twin: Inputs with identical per-unit variance and identical temporal statistics but spatially shuffled channels (xi effectively 0) per sample.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A small linear-Hebbian ring is the minimal form in which weight-space Turing instability exists; it is not a deep network; the non-ML alternative (a continuum field equation for the weight density) is displaced only because the ring is easier to seed-control.
experiments.size: 128 units x 128 inputs, 20000 samples, 5 xi, 5 seeds
stupid_explanations: ring size quantizes wavelength so small shifts look like steps
low-pass smoothing inflates lambda* measured by peak
learning not converged for large xi, giving spurious trend

experiments.hypothesis: A plastic RD medium stores several patterns and recovers a lesioned pattern using stored couplings beyond what border pinning explains.
experiments.mechanism: W1 medium (32x32) with sequential storage of P patterns, each produced by clamped Phase A from a different seed; recall from cue with 20% of cells re-randomized; lesion test removes a 8x8 square.
experiments.intervention: Sweep P in {1,2,3,4,6}; lesion tests on P=1 with couplings inside the lesion intact vs scrambled.
experiments.control: Nearest-neighbour Hopfield network with the same number of plastic edges storing the same binarized patterns.
experiments.positive_control: P=1 with hand-carved couplings (as in W1).
experiments.observable: overlap between recalled and target binarized pattern; recovered bits inside lesion.
experiments.success_criterion: capacity (largest P with mean overlap >= 0.9 over 5 seeds) >= 2; lesion overlap with intact couplings exceeds scrambled-inside by >= 0.2 (paired, 10 seeds, Wilcoxon p<0.01).
experiments.alternative_explanation: Local Hopfield dynamics in disguise; border phase pinning drives repair.
experiments.null_twin: scrambled-inside couplings for lesion test; permuted couplings for recall test.
experiments.why_this_implementation: Keeps memory in transport coefficients of a field; the Hopfield comparison is included as the familiar baseline, not the ontology.
experiments.size: 32x32 grid, 1984 edges, up to 6 patterns, 3000 steps per phase, 5-10 seeds
stupid_explanations: patterns from different seeds share wavelength so overlap floor is high
8x8 lesion below wavelength is refilled by diffusion alone
binarization threshold tuned post hoc

experiments.hypothesis: A timing-asymmetric Hebbian (STDP-like) update of directed transport couplings, driven by morphogen waves that always travel in +x, writes an antisymmetric coupling component aligned with the wave direction; this tissue arrow persists for one decay time after the waves stop and biases the later spread of a released morphogen downstream, beyond what the same coupling magnitudes with scrambled orientation produce.
experiments.mechanism: 48x48 torus of cells. Every edge e from cell i to its +x neighbour j (horizontal) or +y neighbour j (vertical) carries two directed transport rates r_{i->j} = D0*g_e*(1+eps_e) and r_{j->i} = D0*g_e*(1-eps_e); D0 = 1; g_e = exp(0.3*N(0,1)) per edge (RNG stream 0 of the seed), divided by the mean over all edges; g is fixed (not plastic). Plastic variable eps_e in [-0.9, 0.9], starting at 0. Activity u_i(t) in {0,1} is an imposed travelling morphogen wave: u_i(t) = 1 iff ((t - x_i - j_i) mod 48) < 3, speed 1 cell per time unit, width 3 cells, period 48, where j_i ~ N(0, 0.5) is a fixed per-cell timing jitter (RNG stream 6). Traces: dx_i/dt = (u_i - x_i)/tau, tau = 2, x_i(0) = 0. STDP update (treatment): d eps_e/dt = eta*(x_i*u_j - x_j*u_i) - lambda*eps_e, then clip to [-0.9, 0.9]; eta = 0.0866, lambda = 0.01. eta is fixed a priori by the normalization rule 'for jitter-free waves the analytic equilibrium eps equals 0.2' (per passage, integral of x_i*u_j - x_j*u_i = 1.1088 for delay 1, width 3, tau 2; per unit time 1.1088/48; eta = 0.2*lambda*48/1.1088). Morphogen transport of a released pulse: da_i/dt = sum_j r_{j->i}*a_j - sum_j r_{i->j}*a_i (mass conserving). Explicit Euler dt = 0.02 throughout.
experiments.intervention: TREATMENT, per seed: wave epoch 480 time units (10 wave passages) with the STDP update on; quiet epoch 100 time units (= 1/lambda) with u = 0, traces decaying and eps decaying under -lambda*eps (update still applied; with u = 0 it is pure decay); then the pulse test with all couplings frozen: unit mass released at each of 16 release cells (RNG stream 3), transport run for t_test = 8 time units, and the observables read.
experiments.control: Reversed-wave control: identical to the treatment (same g, jitter, traces, STDP rule, schedule, decay, release cells) except the waves travel in -x: u_i(t) = 1 iff ((t + x_i - j_i) mod 48) < 3. If the arrow is written by temporal order it must flip sign (P near -1); if it comes from code orientation (array rolls, update order) it will not. Used by failure clause F4. The eps = 0 medium (FLAT) is the instrument baseline used by F3.
experiments.positive_control: Directed couplings written by hand: horizontal eps_e ~ N(0.2, 0.1) clipped to [-0.9, 0.9] (all pointing downstream on average), vertical eps_e = 0; same g, same release cells, same pulse test.
experiments.observable: P = polarity index over horizontal edges = sum_e A_e / sum_e |A_e| with A_e = r_{i->j} - r_{j->i} = 2*D0*g_e*eps_e (+1 = every edge points downstream along +x, 0 = no net orientation). B = downstream bias of the released pulses at t_test: for each release cell, d = signed torus x-offset of every cell from the release column, in [-24, 23]; B_pulse = mass(d > 0) - mass(d < 0) over total mass; B = mean over the 16 pulses. Diagnostics: P_perp (same index over vertical edges), mean x displacement.

experiments.alternative_explanation: Drift without polarity: a spatial gradient in the symmetric part g along x (e.g. from wave attenuation) biases the centroid of a spreading pulse even with eps = 0; or the implementation's update order (array rolls, sweep direction) leaks asymmetry. Here waves are imposed plane waves on a torus (no attenuation, no source), g is fixed and random without gradient, the null twin keeps g and |eps| exactly, the FLAT check (F3) bounds instrument bias and the reversed-wave control (F4) must flip the arrow.
experiments.null_twin: The treatment's own final coupling field with every eps_e (horizontal and vertical) given an independent fair random sign (RNG stream 2): g and the |eps| histogram identical, orientation relative to the wave destroyed. Same release cells and pulse test.
experiments.substrate: directed transport on a cell lattice (morphogen hopping on a 48x48 torus) driven by imposed travelling morphogen waves
experiments.cost_estimate: controls: about 0.1 CPU core-minute; treatment + reversed-wave control + twin pulse tests: about 1.5 CPU core-minutes (numpy, single core)
stupid_explanations: array-roll or update-order asymmetry in the code writes an arrow by itself (F4 reversed-wave control must flip the arrow; F3 flat couplings bound the pulse instrument)
a gradient in the symmetric couplings g along x produces centroid drift without any antisymmetry (g fixed, gradient-free; the twin keeps g exactly)
torus wrap-around makes downstream and upstream mass ambiguous (t_test = 8 keeps pulse spread well below half the torus; d is measured as the shortest signed offset)
the polarity index is 1 for any tiny but uniform asymmetry, so P alone could pass with a biologically meaningless arrow (S2 and S3 require an effect on transport of a fixed size)
the release cells sit at particular wave phases when waves stop (waves are off for 100 time units before release; release cells random)

experiments.hypothesis: In a reaction-diffusion medium whose activator couplings were shaped by Hebbian co-activity while the pattern formed, a large lesion (24x24 cells, about 3.6 pattern wavelengths across) regrows the ORIGINAL pattern inside the lesion better than (a) the same medium with the couplings inside the lesion scrambled, and (b) an unwritten medium with uniform couplings; i.e. stored couplings carry repair information beyond what the intact border supplies.
experiments.mechanism: Gierer-Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics on a 48x48 torus (periodic in both axes, no boundaries). a_t = sum over the 4 edges e of D0*g_e*(a_j - a_i) + a^2/h - a ; h_t = Dh*lap(h) + mu*(a^2 - h); mu = 2.0, D0 = 0.5, Dh = 10.0, explicit Euler dt = 0.02, a floored at 0, h floored at 1e-6. Homogeneous steady state a = h = 1; Turing wavelength about 6.6 cells. Hebbian coupling plasticity (treatment only, Phase A): every step, for each edge e = (i,j), g_e += dt*[eta*(a_i*a_j/mean(a)^2 - 1) - lambda*(g_e - 1)], then clip g_e to [0.1, 5]; eta = 0.1, lambda = 0.1; mean(a) = spatial mean of a at that step. Plasticity is OFF in every phase except Phase A.
experiments.intervention: TREATMENT, per seed s: Phase A = from a = h = 1 + 0.01*N(0,1) (RNG stream 0 of seed s), 3000 steps WITH plasticity starting from g = 1. Settle = 1500 further steps, plasticity off, on the learned g; the settled activator map is the original O. Lesion = a 24x24 square at a seed-determined position (RNG stream 1, wraps on the torus): a and h inside set to max(1 + 0.3*N(0,1), 0) and max(1 + 0.3*N(0,1), 1e-3) with RNG stream 2. Regrowth = 3000 steps, plasticity off, on the learned g. Observable read on the regrown activator map R.
experiments.control: FIXED medium: g = 1 on every edge throughout; the reference pattern formed from the same initial noise (3000 steps), settled 1500 steps, same lesion position and same lesion noise, 3000 regrowth steps. Pure border pinning in an unwritten medium. Paired with the treatment by seed.
experiments.positive_control: Couplings written by hand from the pattern instead of by Hebbian plasticity: run 3000 steps on g = 1 from the seed's initial noise (reference map); cores = cells with z-scored activator > 1; every edge joining a core cell to a non-core cell gets g = 0.1, every other edge g = 1 (domain boundaries insulated). Then settle 1500 steps on this carved field (original O), lesion, regrow 3000 steps on the same carved field. Effect present by construction: the couplings store where spot boundaries were.
experiments.observable: Recovered information fraction RIF inside the lesion: binarize O and R each at its own whole-field mean; RIF = I_MM(O_bin; R_bin) / H(O_bin), both over the 576 lesion cells, I_MM = Miller-Madow corrected plug-in mutual information in bits, H = plug-in binary entropy of O_bin over the lesion. RIF = 1 when the lesion regrows exactly; RIF about 0 when the regrown pattern is unrelated to the original. Diagnostics (not clause statistics): raw bits, Pearson r inside the lesion, binary agreement.

experiments.alternative_explanation: Border pinning: the intact pattern around the lesion invades the lesion and imposes its phase, so repair would occur in any medium; learned couplings could also simply lower or raise activator diffusion inside the lesion, changing how fast the border front invades versus how fast interior noise nucleates, without storing WHERE spots were. The null twin (same coupling values inside the lesion, rearranged) keeps the second effect and the border; the FIXED control measures pure border pinning.
experiments.null_twin: The treatment's own learned coupling field, with the g values of all edges whose two endpoints both lie inside the lesion randomly permuted among themselves (RNG stream 3); all edges touching the border or outside unchanged; same original O, same lesion, same lesion noise. Coupling-value histogram inside the lesion and the entire border are matched; only the stored spatial arrangement inside the lesion is destroyed.
experiments.substrate: reaction-diffusion (Gierer-Meinhardt on a 48x48 torus with per-edge activator couplings)
experiments.cost_estimate: controls: about 0.25 CPU core-minute; treatment + twin + control arms: about 0.5 CPU core-minute (numpy, single core)

learned couplings only change mean activator diffusion inside the lesion (a wavelength/speed effect, not stored positions); the twin keeps the value histogram, so this effect is shared with the twin
binarization at the whole-field mean makes sparse patterns look recovered by agreement alone (RIF normalizes by the entropy of the original inside the lesion; raw agreement is only a diagnostic)
